title: PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL took 2.4s: check SQLite connection pooling
description:
The gate failure that started this thread:

    WARN sqlx::query: slow statement: execution time exceeded alert
    threshold summary="PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL; …"
    db.statement="\n\nPRAGMA journal_mode = WAL; PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON; \n"
    elapsed=2.414809295s slow_threshold=1s

2.4 seconds for two pragmas. `sigint_during_startup_stops_cleanly`
failed because of it: the server had not printed its ready line inside
the window the test allowed.

## Why it matters past this one failure

`journal_mode` and `foreign_keys` are **per connection**, not per
database. Whatever sets them is therefore on every connection the
process opens. If connections are opened per operation instead of
pooled, every operation pays whatever that 2.4 seconds was, and the
cost shows up as the I/O sensitivity in bead mimid-604m.2.

## What to check

- Where this statement is issued: `mimid-agent-store`, `mimid-server`'s
  store module, and `mimi_mls::Store`, whose SQLite connection callers
  share for their own tables (crate map).
- Whether each of those uses a pool, and whether the pool's
  `after_connect` is what runs the pragmas. A pool that opens
  `max_connections` eagerly pays this once per connection at startup.
- `journal_mode = WAL` is a no-op on a database already in WAL mode but
  still takes the write lock to check. A second connection setting it
  while the first holds the lock waits.
- Whether the agent and the server share one database file through two
  pools in the same process (the test harness runs both).

## Fix shape, if pooling is the answer

Set the pragmas once in the pool's connect options
(`SqliteConnectOptions::journal_mode`/`foreign_keys`), not as a
statement after connecting, so SQLite applies them during open rather
than as a locked write.
